title: Multi-agent skill registry, graph edge, and footgun audit (2026-08-01) -- premises checked, not assumed
notes: Requested as a 4-pass audit with several specific premises pre-asserted (13/13 skill sync, 92 derived_from / 6 claim_links / 83% isolation, footgun numbers #3/#9/#10/#26). Each premise was checked against the actual filesystem/graph rather than reported back verbatim -- some held, some did not, one could not be verified in the form asked.

PASS 1 (skills): .claude/skills/ (the real project-skill loader location, per harness_skill_registry_repair_20260731_correction) and .agents/skills/ (the doc-referenced source) both hold the same 13 directories, name-for-name identical (`diff` on directory listings: empty). .gemini/config/skills/ (Gemini CLI's own separate mirror) holds the 7 pre-canonicalization flat skills (lfp, spiking, tfr, nwb-io, visualization, functional-connectivity, progress-review-plan) plus papers-librarian and labyrinth-protocol. 6 of those 7 carry an explicit 'DEPRECATED -- superseded by .agents/skills/<name>' redirect in their frontmatter description. progress-review-plan does NOT: it still holds full, undeprecated PRP-loop content in the Gemini mirror, even though the Claude-side copies (.agents and .claude) were deleted outright per harness_skill_registry_repair_20260731_correction's own notes. This is real drift between the two CLIs' skill sets, not resolved by this audit.

PASS 2 (graph): the per-file artifacts/.lab/*.json documents mostly do NOT carry inline edge arrays (only 30/313 files have any 'links'/'edges' field at all) -- the real compiled adjacency lives in labyrinth_unified.json (compiled 2026-07-27, header claims node_count=274). That file's 'nodes' array actually has 279 entries; 5 lack an 'id' field entirely (one is a daemon_config-shaped blob with no node semantics at all) -- excluding those, exactly 274 valid nodes remain, matching the header. Edge relation counts across those 274 nodes' generated.links: refines 290, supports 490, derives_from 178, contradicts 6, belongs_to 40, contains 4, relates_to 12, questions 7 (1027 edges total). There is no relation literally named 'claim_links' in this schema, so the requested premise of '92 derived_from / 6 claim_links / 83% isolated' does not map cleanly onto the graph as compiled now -- it may describe an earlier snapshot (the source doctrine node, labyrinth_patch_20260725_v16_doctrine, is dated 2026-07-25/confirmed 2026-07-28, and derives_from has since grown to 178) or a metric computed a different way. Reported as a discrepancy, not silently reconciled to the requested number.

PASS 2 (dangling edges, found independently, not part of the original ask): 40 edges across 8 nodes (all omission-*/papers-mission-adjacent context nodes) target an id literally 'mission', which does not exist in the compiled graph -- 'papers-mission' does exist and is very likely the intended target, suggesting a truncated-id bug at edge-authoring time. Not present in the 2026-07-29 graph_health_audit's 'zero dangling edges' finding because that scan only covered the 296 per-file JSON documents' own inline edge arrays, not labyrinth_unified.json's compiled links -- the two dangling-edge scans covered different graph representations and neither alone is complete.

PASS 2 (aperture/dark region): 37/274 nodes (13.5%) carry zero outgoing links in the compiled graph -- this is the only aperture-shaped number this audit can support with a direct count. The 7-term J objective function, its completeness score, and 'contradiction: not measured' framing from the v16 doctrine patch were read and are consistent with what CLAUDE.md's Labyrinth Reflex section describes, but this audit did not re-run or recompute J itself -- no receipt for a live J value is claimed here.

PASS 3 (footguns): all four requested footgun numbers (#3 dual-area probe mapping, #9 get_spike_times index-vs-column, #10 h5py byte-string coercion, #26 DOCX ascending figure order) exist in .agents/AGENTS.md exactly as numbered and described -- the premise was accurate, not fabricated. Live compliance spot-checks: #3 -- grep for the naive `location.split(',')[0]` pattern found zero live occurrences outside a comment in scripts/archive_oneoff/ that explicitly references the already-fixed bug; clean. #9 -- no `get_spike_times(` call pattern indexing a `unit_id` column found in current jnwb/scripts/context paths; clean. #10 -- byte-aware coercion helpers are present in jnwb/__init__.py, the canonical location; present as expected. #26 -- no active script uses the documented `insert(idx_before_next_figure, ...)` remedy by name, but the one currently-active whole-manuscript embedder inspected (scripts/finalize_master_manuscript.py) sidesteps the footgun structurally: it inserts each figure's image directly before that figure's own pre-existing caption paragraph (already in document order), rather than appending then reordering, so the footgun class does not apply to that script's method. Not exhaustively checked across all ~10 active docx-touching scripts in scripts/ -- only the one sampled.

SVG-to-PNG rendering claim (from the request) was not checked: no evidence was gathered on which renderer (headless Chrome/Edge vs matplotlib's own PNG export vs cairosvg) each figure script actually uses. This session's own fig02/03/04 work exports PNG directly from matplotlib figures (fig.savefig), never through an SVG-to-PNG conversion step, and a cairosvg install on this machine was found to be non-functional (missing libcairo-2.dll) earlier in this session -- so any script that DOES depend on cairosvg for SVG->PNG would currently fail outright, not silently drop content. Not verified further; flagged as unchecked rather than reported pass/fail.
issues: progress-review-plan is deleted on the Claude side (.agents, .claude) but still live and undeprecated on the Gemini side (.gemini/config/skills/) -- a genuine cross-CLI drift, unresolved by this audit.
40 dangling edges in labyrinth_unified.json target a nonexistent 'mission' id, likely meant to be 'papers-mission' -- unresolved, no edges were rewritten by this audit.

The requested '92 derived_from / 6 claim_links / 83% isolated' premise does not match a direct count against the current compiled graph (178 derives_from edges, no claim_links relation type, 13.5% zero-outdegree nodes) -- the discrepancy is reported, not silently resolved to either number.
DOCX footgun #26 compliance was spot-checked on one active script only, not the full set of ~10 docx-touching scripts in scripts/.
SVG-to-PNG renderer claim from the request was not investigated at all.
plan: If cross-CLI skill parity is wanted, either deprecate progress-review-plan in .gemini/config/skills/ to match the Claude-side deletion, or restore it on the Claude side -- a decision for the user, not silently picked here.
Fix or remove the 40 'mission'-targeting dangling edges in labyrinth_unified.json (likely a rename to 'papers-mission'), then recompile/re-verify dangling-edge count.

Re-derive the actual source of the '92 derived_from / 6 claim_links' figures (check labyrinth_unified.json's compiled_at history or any prior compilation snapshot) before treating either number as current.
Extend the footgun #26 spot-check to the remaining active docx scripts if DOCX figure-ordering correctness matters for an upcoming manuscript pass.

verification.receipt: All counts above come from direct `python -c` scans of labyrinth_unified.json and grep against jnwb/scripts/.agents/.claude/.gemini paths run in this session, not recalled or assumed. Diff of .claude/skills vs .agents/skills directory listings was empty (identical names). Footgun text matched grep of .agents/AGENTS.md lines 39-120 verbatim against the four requested numbers.

links.reasoning: That node's '92 derived_from / 6 claim_links / 83% isolated' figures do not reproduce against a fresh count of the current compiled graph (178 derives_from, no claim_links relation type, 13.5% isolated) -- either the graph grew substantially since 2026-07-25/28, or the metric was computed differently. Flagged rather than silently reconciled.
Independently re-verified this session: .claude/skills/ and .agents/skills/ hold identical 13-name sets, confirming the 2026-07-31 fix is still in effect as of 2026-08-01.

Both are dangling-edge scans of artifacts/.lab/, but cover different graph representations (per-file inline edges vs labyrinth_unified.json's compiled links) and neither is a superset of the other -- the 2026-07-29 audit's 'zero dangling edges' claim is correct for its own scope and does not extend to the 40 found here.
